# Panels worker: review, challenge and controller pages (viewer UX slice S4c)

## Goal

An operator who opens a review, challenge, handoff, approval or integrate node in the Projects viewer sees in the first screen what was decided, what blocks, how long it took and what to do next, without scanning a table. Implement slice S4c of `docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md`: section 4.7 (Review), 4.8 (Challenge) and 4.9 (Handoff, approval, integrate) are the specification; section 11 lists the slice; sections 12.2 and 12.3 are its tests. `decisions.md` in this feature records the operator's decisions.

## Context

- Steps 1 to 4 of the redesign are merged: the node shell (`src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx` dispatcher, `NodeHeader.tsx`, `SectionIndex.tsx`, `useRunData.ts`) and the per-kind section files in `src/projects/node/`. You fill in `node/ReviewSections.tsx`, `node/ChallengeSections.tsx` and `node/ControllerSections.tsx`; the header, attempt strip and `node-next` already come from the shell.
- Time: use `time.ts` (`formatClock`, `formatAgo`, `formatSpan`, `spanBetween`), `Time.tsx` and `useNow`. The next action and commands come from `deriveNow` in `contracts/projects/triage.ts` and `CommandBlock.tsx`; read them, do not edit them.
- Fixtures: `tests/project-workflows/fixtures/ux-review.ts` is an empty module already registered by `fixtures/index.ts` (read that file for the payload and `seed` shape, and `ux-verify.ts` or `ux-launch.ts` for a filled example). Browser helpers, including `attach(page, testInfo, id)`, are in `tests/project-workflows/support.ts`.
- Handoffs of earlier slices: `docs/handoff/ux-s4core.md`, `ux-s4a.md`, `ux-s4b.md` (conventions, red/green evidence format).

## Constraints

- Only edit the paths your lane owns in the pinned policy. You own `src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx` and `src/projects/node/model.ts` so that NodeDetail passes what it already holds (`inputs`, node events, `timeline`, the clock, `node`, `now`) to the review, challenge and controller sections and builds their section-index entries; the sections never fetch or poll on their own and never call `useNow` (one clock at RunView, PRD 5.3). Change NodeDetail only for these kinds; worker and verify pages stay as they are. The `lists` lane owns `ProjectsView.tsx`, `api.ts`, `NowBanner.tsx`, `CommandBlock.tsx`, `LiveStatus.tsx`, `projects.spec.ts` and the list files; do not edit them or read its worktree. Put pure helpers in `src/projects/node/panels.ts` (no React import: the unit tests import it) and their tests in `tests/unit/panels.test.ts`, which the `test:unit` glob already collects.
- The viewer stays read-only: every button text is one of those listed at the end of PRD 12.3, and no button text holds a path or a command. Keep `expectNoExecutionControls` green.
- Keep every existing scenario passing, in particular `reviewers.spec.ts:86` (all five findings column headers on a multi-valued review) and `review.spec.ts`.
- Reviewer times only from served fields: a duration from `launched_at` to `accepted_at`; nothing when `launched_at` is null. A review serves reviewers only once it is decided (`review.json` is written on the verdict), so no live per-reviewer elapsed time or deadline is shown; the running review node's own span comes from the shell header. Never invent a time.
- If the PRD is ambiguous, choose, record the choice as an open assumption, and keep going.

## Acceptance

- Fixtures in `ux-review.ts` for both phases: a native review decided with two approved reviewers and their durations, a native review blocked by one reviewer while the other is `pending` with `launched_at` set, a print review blocked by a P1, a challenge that passed on attempt 3 with P2 notes, a paused challenge with one P1, and a succeeded approval with no event beside a handoff with launch receipts.
- One browser test per scenario id in `tests/project-workflows/ux-review.spec.ts`, each title containing `[scenario:<id>]` and attaching `screenshot:<id>`: `review-blocking-first`, `challenge-headline`, `controller-panels`, asserting what the pinned policy describes, in both phases.
- Unit tests for the pure helpers (deadline and duration, headline wording, wait from receipts).
- Red first: run the new tests against the pre-change code and record that they fail for the right reason; then green. Write `docs/handoff/ux-s4c.md` with what shipped, both runs and any deviation from the PRD.
- Run targeted tests only: `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsx --test tests/unit/panels.test.ts`, and the browser spec files you added or changed with `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker` and with `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate`. The verifier runs every policy check on your snapshot and on the combined candidate. Report exactly what you ran, with results.

# Decisions: viewer-ux-panels-lists

From the grill session of 2026-09-27 with the operator.

## Decisions

- Runs home's Recent section lists every finished run of the last 7 days across all projects, newest first, with no count cap: the `lists` lane filters on `activity.finished_at` (else `updated_at`), and `runs-home` asserts a run older than 7 days is absent from Recent while it stays on its project page.
- No client fan-out fallback: the `lists` lane reads the served `activity` only. A run without `activity` shows `<Status> · updated <time>` with no finish time, no duration and no Needs-you grouping, and no run detail is fetched to reconstruct it.
- The operator's live registry will serve run directories (`viewer.expose_run_dir` for `project-b` and `md-manager`) after this run lands: the `lists` lane only reads `run_dir`; it changes no registry file outside the test harness, and its fixtures set the key in their own temp registry.
- After design challenge attempt 1 of viewer-ux-panels-lists-001 (P1: the sections cannot get the data they need), the `panels` lane owns `src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx`, `src/projects/node/model.ts` and `tests/unit/model.test.ts`: NodeDetail passes inputs, events, timeline, clock and node to the sections, and pure helpers in `src/projects/node/panels.ts` compute the headline, wait, approval instant and deadline wording.
- Tests that the other lane's fixtures can change assert only on their own run ids: `runs-home` never asserts whole-section counts (`Needs you · N`, `Running · N`, 'nothing is running') or the full contents of Recent, because the combined candidate also lists the `panels` lane's runs; the `panels` lane asserts commands with `toContainText` on `node-next`, not on `CommandBlock`'s inner structure.
- Time-dependent text (a running reviewer's elapsed time and deadline, the 7-day Recent window, the 15 s controller debounce) is tested with `page.clock` set to a fixed instant, as `ux-time.spec.ts` does, in both phases; a deadline already passed reads `deadline <time> (passed)`.

- After design challenge attempt 1 of viewer-ux-panels-lists-002 (P1: a live review serves no reviewers): the per-reviewer live elapsed time and deadline of PRD 4.7 are deferred until the controller serves reviewer receipts during the wait; `review-blocking-first` covers decided and print reviews and a `pending` reviewer with no ticking clock.
- The blocking card sits outside `review-findings` and carries no `finding` test id; narrow widths restyle the one findings DOM as cards (no second copy), so every existing `finding` count in `review.spec.ts`, `lanes.spec.ts`, `inputs.spec.ts`, `reviewers.spec.ts` and `clarity.spec.ts` stays unchanged.
- NodeDetail reads the review through the run cache (`useRunReview` in `useRunData.ts`, as RunView does) and passes it down for the section-index counts and the approval's bundle hash; `ReviewPanel` stops fetching on its own. "Never fetch on their own" means no request the run cache does not already make.
- `served-activity` asserts 'controller running' only in the worker phase (mocks); in the candidate phase a seeded PID gives `not_running`, and the test asserts the 15 s debounce with `page.clock.install` and `fastForward` (not `setFixedTime`, under which 15 s never pass).
- Runs home gets its rows from the run lists: projects, then workflows, then each workflow's runs, paging until `updated_at` falls below the 7-day cutoff, polled every 15 s. "No fan-out" means no per-run detail request: every row renders from the run summary's served `activity`. The handoff records the request count.

## Assumptions

- `contracts/projects/triage.ts` (`deriveNow`) and `contracts/projects/v1.ts` are read-only for both lanes; a wording or field that seems missing is recorded in the lane's handoff as a follow-up, not added.
- Needs you lists runs whose `activity.attention.kind` is `question`, `pane` or `approval`; Running lists non-terminal runs not already in Needs you; a run appears in one section only.
- Reviewer deadlines use `inputs.automatic.review_timeout_seconds` and carry `≈`; with `launched_at` null the `panels` lane shows "launch time not recorded" and no deadline.
- Both lanes keep every existing test id; new test ids follow the PRD's names where it gives one.

## Deferred

- The one-request list endpoint (PRD B4) and the evidence detail fields (B5).
- Slice S7 (Assignment reorder, review diff inline): the separate feature `viewer-ux-depth` after this run is integrated.
- Controller and exporter follow-ups C1 to C10 of PRD section 9.4.

# Decisions: viewer-ux-panels-lists

From the grill session of 2026-09-27 with the operator.

## Decisions

- Runs home's Recent section lists every finished run of the last 7 days across all projects, newest first, with no count cap: the `lists` lane filters on `activity.finished_at` (else `updated_at`), and `runs-home` asserts a run older than 7 days is absent from Recent while it stays on its project page.
- No client fan-out fallback: the `lists` lane reads the served `activity` only. A run without `activity` shows `<Status> · updated <time>` with no finish time, no duration and no Needs-you grouping, and no run detail is fetched to reconstruct it.
- The operator's live registry will serve run directories (`viewer.expose_run_dir` for `project-b` and `md-manager`) after this run lands: the `lists` lane only reads `run_dir`; it changes no registry file outside the test harness, and its fixtures set the key in their own temp registry.
- After design challenge attempt 1 of viewer-ux-panels-lists-001 (P1: the sections cannot get the data they need), the `panels` lane owns `src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx`, `src/projects/node/model.ts` and `tests/unit/model.test.ts`: NodeDetail passes inputs, events, timeline, clock and node to the sections, and pure helpers in `src/projects/node/panels.ts` compute the headline, wait, approval instant and deadline wording.
- Tests that the other lane's fixtures can change assert only on their own run ids: `runs-home` never asserts whole-section counts (`Needs you · N`, `Running · N`, 'nothing is running') or the full contents of Recent, because the combined candidate also lists the `panels` lane's runs; the `panels` lane asserts commands with `toContainText` on `node-next`, not on `CommandBlock`'s inner structure.
- Time-dependent text (a running reviewer's elapsed time and deadline, the 7-day Recent window, the 15 s controller debounce) is tested with `page.clock` set to a fixed instant, as `ux-time.spec.ts` does, in both phases; a deadline already passed reads `deadline <time> (passed)`.

- After design challenge attempt 1 of viewer-ux-panels-lists-002 (P1: a live review serves no reviewers): the per-reviewer live elapsed time and deadline of PRD 4.7 are deferred until the controller serves reviewer receipts during the wait; `review-blocking-first` covers decided and print reviews and a `pending` reviewer with no ticking clock.
- The blocking card sits outside `review-findings` and carries no `finding` test id; narrow widths restyle the one findings DOM as cards (no second copy), so every existing `finding` count in `review.spec.ts`, `lanes.spec.ts`, `inputs.spec.ts`, `reviewers.spec.ts` and `clarity.spec.ts` stays unchanged.
- NodeDetail reads the review through the run cache (`useRunReview` in `useRunData.ts`, as RunView does) and passes it down for the section-index counts and the approval's bundle hash; `ReviewPanel` stops fetching on its own. "Never fetch on their own" means no request the run cache does not already make.
- `served-activity` asserts 'controller running' only in the worker phase (mocks); in the candidate phase a seeded PID gives `not_running`, and the test asserts the 15 s debounce with `page.clock.install` and `fastForward` (not `setFixedTime`, under which 15 s never pass).
- Runs home gets its rows from the run lists: projects, then workflows, then each workflow's runs, paging until `updated_at` falls below the 7-day cutoff, polled every 15 s. "No fan-out" means no per-run detail request: every row renders from the run summary's served `activity`. The handoff records the request count.

## Assumptions

- `contracts/projects/triage.ts` (`deriveNow`) and `contracts/projects/v1.ts` are read-only for both lanes; a wording or field that seems missing is recorded in the lane's handoff as a follow-up, not added.
- Needs you lists runs whose `activity.attention.kind` is `question`, `pane` or `approval`; Running lists non-terminal runs not already in Needs you; a run appears in one section only.
- Reviewer deadlines use `inputs.automatic.review_timeout_seconds` and carry `≈`; with `launched_at` null the `panels` lane shows "launch time not recorded" and no deadline.
- Both lanes keep every existing test id; new test ids follow the PRD's names where it gives one.

## Deferred

- The one-request list endpoint (PRD B4) and the evidence detail fields (B5).
- Slice S7 (Assignment reorder, review diff inline): the separate feature `viewer-ux-depth` after this run is integrated.
- Controller and exporter follow-ups C1 to C10 of PRD section 9.4.

 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

1 # PRD: Workflow viewer UX ("Run Story") 2 3 Status: Proposed 2026-09-24. Synthesizes the four-lens audit of the Projects viewer (orientation, chronology, detail-density, live-status; screenshots `shots/01`–`14`, payloads `api/*.json`), three redesign proposals (timeline-first, triage-first, graph-inspector) and two judges' verdicts. Both judges picked **timeline-first** as the base. This PRD adds every graft that fits and respects every `must_avoid`. Where the two judges disagree, Appendix B records the decision. Follows [PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md](PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md), [PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md](PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md), [PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md](PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md) and [PRD_WORKER_LANES.md](PRD_WORKER_LANES.md) (all in `docs/`; this file is meant to land as `docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md`). Their truthfulness rules still hold. This PRD changes only how compactly they are said. 4 5 Revision 2 (2026-09-24) closes the critic's gaps. The changes, each checked against the code: 6 - Node-level interruptions (review, freeze) and repair continuations now get a next step (6.2 rule 5). 7 - A new situation covers runs the controller blocked before freeze (6.2 rule 6, reason source 0, B1). 8 - Pane attention is carried everywhere a question is (6.4, B2 `attention.kind: 'pane'`). 9 - Controller liveness is read-only and PID-reuse safe (B2 `activity.controller`). 10 - The first-screen budget is measured against a one-row Projects header, with the tabs above the graph (4.2). 11 - Slices are file-disjoint when run in parallel, and no slice's test depends on a later slice (11, 12). 12 - B3 moves to a top-level `viewer` key, which survives re-registration. 13 - Test migrations are corrected (12.3). The `answer`, `init` and `status` command wording is fixed, gate reasons without a check id are handled, and two API field claims are corrected. 14 15 Scope: `src/projects/**`, `src/App.tsx` (Projects header only), `src/App.css` and new per-area stylesheets, `tests/project-workflows/**` and `tests/unit/**`. For backend slice S5: `server/projects.ts`, `server/projectsConfig.ts`, `contracts/projects/**` and a new pure module `contracts/projects/triage.ts`. The Python controller (`workflow/*.py`) is **not** changed here. Controller-side gaps are listed as follow-ups C1–C10 (section 9.4). The viewer stays strictly read-only. It never runs a command and never mutates a run. 16 17 ## 1. Problem 18 19 The user's complaint, verbatim: *"Lets work on making the UX better for the workflow section. Its not good, i need to look around to understand whats where when it happened and overall is just bad."* 20 21 The audit confirms each part of the sentence with measurements taken from the live runs. 22 23 **"what's where": nothing answers the operator's question where they land.** 24 - The run page spends its first screen on an 11-fact grid, a 3-sentence legend, a keyboard hint, a duplicate node list and an empty "Select a node…" panel (`04-…-fold.png`, RunView.tsx:98-217). It never names the failing step, the reason or the next command (orientation:run-first-screen-no-answer, live-status:run-why-not-surfaced). 25 - For skeleton-001, the cause ("general blocked: 1 P1, Private matches can be joined without their code") takes a click and about 1.3 screens of scrolling to reach. For workflow-guardrails-001 it sits inside Candidate › Lane ui › error box. 26 - No page tells the operator which CLI command to run next (live-status:no-next-action). 27 28 **"when it happened": the run has no history view.** 29 - Events render only per node, at the bottom of each node page (NodeDetail.tsx:466-487). 30 - Events whose `node_id` is null are dropped everywhere (NodeDetail.tsx:305). In skeleton-001 that is 7 of 26 events, including the controller's diagnosis *"failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 … a code fix is a lane repair (RUNBOOK)"* and *"Repair 1 applied"* (chronology:unattributed-events-hidden, live-status:controller-events-hidden). 31 - No duration is ever computed. Every time is a full UTC ISO string (status.ts:100-104). "Last event" is shown as a sequence number, and "Updated" trails real activity by 3.5 minutes (orientation:no-run-timeline, chronology:no-durations, chronology:last-activity-misleading, chronology:utc-only-absolute-times). 32 33 **"look around": node pages are walls.** 34 - `launch_game` is 19,834 px tall. 77 file panels take 15,400 px of it, and the Markdown files are auto-rendered (detail-density:launch-files-wall). 35 - A worker question sits at y≈19,320 (orientation:pending-question-buried). 36 - On `verify_game` the gate sits behind a repeated worker summary and 10 assumptions (detail-density:worker-narrative-duplicated). 37 - Earlier failed attempts are served by the API (`results/game/1` and `/2` return 200) but cannot be reached from the viewer (orientation:earlier-attempts-unreachable). 38 - The node list wastes a third of the width for the whole page. The graph clips "Integrate candidate" at 1440 px (orientation:navigation-model-node-list, orientation:graph-clipped). 39 - At 390 px the node detail starts at y≈1,975 and the verify page overflows to 427 px wide (orientation:mobile-node-detail-offscreen). 40 41 **"overall just bad": live watching is not trustworthy.** 42 - A worker waiting on a question, or blocked in its pane on a permission prompt or a refusal, looks exactly like a busy one (live-status:question-attention-invisible). 43 - Polling is silent, and a failed poll keeps stale data with no warning. A dead controller cannot be told from a quiet one: during a worker phase, 28 minutes without events is normal (live-status:no-liveness-indicator). 44 - A run the controller stopped before freeze, or interrupted during review or freeze, shows no cause and no command. Its reason is only in a node-less controller row that no page renders (live-status:run-why-not-surfaced, live-status:no-next-action). 45 - Every workflow is titled "Feature implementation" (orientation:naming-feature-implementation). 46 - Reaching a run takes three clicks through near-empty pages (orientation:hierarchy-depth-empty-levels). 47 48 All 23 P1 findings fall into these four themes. Appendix A maps all 72 findings. 49 50 ## 2. Goals and non-goals 51 52 ### Goals 53 54 1. **Answer first.** The first screen of a run page, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, answers five questions: 55 - Where is the run, or where did it stop? 56 - Why? 57 - Since when? 58 - What exactly do I type next, if anything? 59 - Is this page current? 60 2. **One story in time.** At 1440×900 the first screen also shows the Steps table: each step's start, duration and attempt markers. The markers include ⚑ (the controller's diagnosis) and ⚒ (an operator repair) on the step they concern. 61 - The full text of the node-less diagnosis and repair rows is in Activity, directly below Steps on the same default tab, never behind a toggle or a tab. 62 - The guarantee covers runs with up to 2 lanes: every live run so far, and every fixture except `RUN_THREE_LANES`. For those runs the focus step's row is inside the fold; section 4.2 has the measured budget. 63 - With 3 or more lanes the graph grows a row and the focus row can fall below the fold. The Now banner still names the focus step there. 64 - At 390×844 the first screen holds the Now banner, and Steps follow directly. 65 3. **One home per piece of evidence.** Each piece of evidence is shown once, where it answers its question: files on the worker, checks, logs and screenshots on verification, findings on review. Everywhere else it appears as a one-line link or a count. 66 4. **Short node pages.** A node page's first screen shows its verdict, timing, attempts and a section index with counts. Long lists are collapsed and fetch their content only on demand. No node page needs more than about 3 screens before the operator expands something. 67 5. **Live-watch trust.** A freshness chip is always visible. 68 - While a run is running or paused, the chip also says whether its controller process is alive (B2 `activity.controller`; Linux `/proc`, and "unknown" elsewhere). 69 - A worker or reviewer that waits on the operator is visible on the run page, the graph, the Steps and strip rows, the run lists and the browser tab title. That covers a waiting question and a pane that needs attention. 70 6. **Honesty kept, said once.** The rules survive: a worker's success is not workflow completion, a worker's report is as signalled and not verified, the viewer is read-only, executors are marked, inferred times are marked. Each is said once, compactly. 71 7. **Shippable slices.** The existing browser suite stays green in both phases (worker mocks and candidate seeds), apart from assertions this PRD migrates explicitly in the same slice. 72 73 ### Non-goals 74 75 - Starting, answering, approving, retrying, repairing or cancelling anything from the viewer. Commands are shown as text to copy. 76 - Changing the controller, exporter or event vocabulary (`workflow/*.py`). Those gaps are follow-ups C1–C10. Until they land, the viewer infers the missing values and labels every inference. 77 - A liveness claim from PID existence alone, such as `process.kill(pid, 0)` on a PID parsed from event text. PID reuse would give a false "alive". 78 - B2 instead reads `/proc//cmdline` and the process start time. It says "running" only for this run's own `automatic-step` child, started before it logged its PID. It says "unknown" whenever it cannot tell. 79 - A controller heartbeat (C7) would make this portable. 80 - The Pi/Claude skills areas. 81 - Renaming `definition.name`. It feeds `definition_revision` (server/projectsConfig.ts:89-90), so changing it would flag every old run as "definition changed". 82 83 ### Confirmed decisions 84 85 - **The SVG graph stays.** It is fitted to the width by retuning `dag.ts`, not rebuilt as HTML. `.workflow-node-meta`, the aria-label format, `.workflow-node-shape` `stroke-dasharray`, `.is-agent`/`.is-controller` and arrow-key roving are unchanged (clarity.spec.ts:63-109, projects.spec.ts:164-168). 86 - **A one-row Projects header.** On Projects routes the app header is one 48 px row: title, the Pi/Claude/Projects roots and Refresh. The Pi/Claude subtitle is dropped there. The breadcrumb is the only other chrome (28 px). Today the chrome takes about 150 px, or about 180 px with the info line (`04-…-fold.png`). The skills routes keep their header. 87 - **Tabs above the graph.** `[Run] [Assignment]` sit directly under the Now banner. The graph lives inside the Run tabpanel, so it disappears on Assignment and comes back on Run (inputs.spec.ts:56, :89). 88 - **One pipeline view per screen.** On the run page, the graph shows *shape and status* and the Steps table shows *time*. The Steps table is the `run-node-list`, not "the same graph as text". On node pages a sticky step strip replaces the graph, so the graph and the strip never share a screen. There are no lane cards that repeat step durations. 89 - **Views that need a link live in the path.** Tabs and attempts are URL path segments (`/assignment`, `/nodes//attempts/`), because App routing is pathname-only (App.tsx:159). 90 - **Section index, not sub-tabs, on node pages.** Evidence stays in the DOM, Ctrl-F works, and most `toBeVisible` assertions survive. 91 - **Commands follow the RUNBOOK**: `"$PY" -m workflow "$RUN" …`. 92 - `$RUN` stays a placeholder unless a workflow opts into serving its run directory (B3, home-relative, off by default). 93 - A command appears only when a situation rule in section 6 matches the run's *current* state. Otherwise the viewer says "No known next step matched" and links the RUNBOOK section. 94 - **The vocabulary is "attempt"**, the word the controller, CLI and RUNBOOK use. The following wordings are retired: "Graph attempt", "Result attempt 3 (graph node attempt is 1)" and "attempt 0". 95 - **Default times are local**, with the UTC value in the tooltip. A remembered Local/UTC toggle is available. 96 97 ## 3. Information architecture 98 99 ### 3.1 Routes 100 101 `routes.ts` gains three literals. `parseProjectsPathname`, which today rejects any trailing segment (routes.ts:82), accepts `assignment` after a run id (added in S3) and `attempts/` after a node id (added in S4-core). Every URL that works today keeps working. 102 103 | Route | Page | First question it answers | 104 |---|---|---| 105 | `/projects` | **Runs home** | Does anything need me, what is running, what finished recently (all projects)? The only page that carries the read-only note (`projects-info`). | 106 | `/projects/

/workflows/` | Feature runs | Run rows (`run-list`) with where each run stands, its duration and its age. "Current definition" moves into a closed `

`, which is open when there are no runs. | 108 | `/…/runs/` | **Run page** (Run tab, default) | Run header → Now banner → lanes line (2+ lanes) → tabs → Run tabpanel: fitted graph, Steps (with times), Activity. | 109 | `/…/runs//assignment` | Run page, Assignment tab (now routed) | What the run was asked to do. | 110 | `/…/runs//nodes/` | **Node view**, latest attempt | Verdict, timing, attempts and next step. Evidence sits behind a section index. | 111 | `/…/runs//nodes//attempts/` | Node view, attempt *k* | That attempt's own result (`results//`, `results/candidate_/`). | 112 113 ### 3.2 What moves where 114 115 | Item | Today (where the audit found it) | New home | Elsewhere | 116 |---|---|---|---| 117 | Failing or active step, reason, next command | nowhere; event #20 at y≈4,600 of 07 | Now banner | the focus node's header | 118 | Run history, incl. `node_id: null` events | per node, at the bottom; node-less events never shown | Run tab: Steps (per node) and Activity (chronological) | node History (filtered) | 119 | 11 run facts | grid at y≈200-490 (RunView.tsx:98-131) | Header facts line plus the `Details ▸` disclosure | Assignment keeps one summary line | 120 | Node list | left third of the page (App.css:345) | Run page: the Steps table. Page designs 150 151 Wireframes use the real runs. Times in the wireframes are UTC, which is what a viewer in UTC would see. # PRD: Workflow viewer UX ("Run Story") Status: Proposed 2026-09-24. Synthesizes the four-lens audit of the Projects viewer (orientation, chronology, detail-density, live-status; screenshots `shots/01`–`14`, payloads `api/*.json`), three redesign proposals (timeline-first, triage-first, graph-inspector) and two judges' verdicts. Both judges picked **timeline-first** as the base. This PRD adds every graft that fits and respects every `must_avoid`. Where the two judges disagree, Appendix B records the decision. Follows [PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md](PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY.md), [PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md](PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md), [PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md](PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md) and [PRD_WORKER_LANES.md](PRD_WORKER_LANES.md) (all in `docs/`; this file is meant to land as `docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md`). Their truthfulness rules still hold. This PRD changes only how compactly they are said. Revision 2 (2026-09-24) closes the critic's gaps. The changes, each checked against the code: - Node-level interruptions (review, freeze) and repair continuations now get a next step (6.2 rule 5). - A new situation covers runs the controller blocked before freeze (6.2 rule 6, reason source 0, B1). - Pane attention is carried everywhere a question is (6.4, B2 `attention.kind: 'pane'`). - Controller liveness is read-only and PID-reuse safe (B2 `activity.controller`). - The first-screen budget is measured against a one-row Projects header, with the tabs above the graph (4.2). - Slices are file-disjoint when run in parallel, and no slice's test depends on a later slice (11, 12). - B3 moves to a top-level `viewer` key, which survives re-registration. - Test migrations are corrected (12.3). The `answer`, `init` and `status` command wording is fixed, gate reasons without a check id are handled, and two API field claims are corrected. Scope: `src/projects/**`, `src/App.tsx` (Projects header only), `src/App.css` and new per-area stylesheets, `tests/project-workflows/**` and `tests/unit/**`. For backend slice S5: `server/projects.ts`, `server/projectsConfig.ts`, `contracts/projects/**` and a new pure module `contracts/projects/triage.ts`. The Python controller (`workflow/*.py`) is **not** changed here. Controller-side gaps are listed as follow-ups C1–C10 (section 9.4). The viewer stays strictly read-only. It never runs a command and never mutates a run. ## 1. Problem The user's complaint, verbatim: *"Lets work on making the UX better for the workflow section. Its not good, i need to look around to understand whats where when it happened and overall is just bad."* The audit confirms each part of the sentence with measurements taken from the live runs. **"what's where": nothing answers the operator's question where they land.** - The run page spends its first screen on an 11-fact grid, a 3-sentence legend, a keyboard hint, a duplicate node list and an empty "Select a node…" panel (`04-…-fold.png`, RunView.tsx:98-217). It never names the failing step, the reason or the next command (orientation:run-first-screen-no-answer, live-status:run-why-not-surfaced). - For skeleton-001, the cause ("general blocked: 1 P1, Private matches can be joined without their code") takes a click and about 1.3 screens of scrolling to reach. For workflow-guardrails-001 it sits inside Candidate › Lane ui › error box. - No page tells the operator which CLI command to run next (live-status:no-next-action). **"when it happened": the run has no history view.** - Events render only per node, at the bottom of each node page (NodeDetail.tsx:466-487). - Events whose `node_id` is null are dropped everywhere (NodeDetail.tsx:305). In skeleton-001 that is 7 of 26 events, including the controller's diagnosis *"failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 … a code fix is a lane repair (RUNBOOK)"* and *"Repair 1 applied"* (chronology:unattributed-events-hidden, live-status:controller-events-hidden). - No duration is ever computed. Every time is a full UTC ISO string (status.ts:100-104). "Last event" is shown as a sequence number, and "Updated" trails real activity by 3.5 minutes (orientation:no-run-timeline, chronology:no-durations, chronology:last-activity-misleading, chronology:utc-only-absolute-times). **"look around": node pages are walls.** - `launch_game` is 19,834 px tall. 77 file panels take 15,400 px of it, and the Markdown files are auto-rendered (detail-density:launch-files-wall). - A worker question sits at y≈19,320 (orientation:pending-question-buried). - On `verify_game` the gate sits behind a repeated worker summary and 10 assumptions (detail-density:worker-narrative-duplicated). - Earlier failed attempts are served by the API (`results/game/1` and `/2` return 200) but cannot be reached from the viewer (orientation:earlier-attempts-unreachable). - The node list wastes a third of the width for the whole page. The graph clips "Integrate candidate" at 1440 px (orientation:navigation-model-node-list, orientation:graph-clipped). - At 390 px the node detail starts at y≈1,975 and the verify page overflows to 427 px wide (orientation:mobile-node-detail-offscreen). **"overall just bad": live watching is not trustworthy.** - A worker waiting on a question, or blocked in its pane on a permission prompt or a refusal, looks exactly like a busy one (live-status:question-attention-invisible). - Polling is silent, and a failed poll keeps stale data with no warning. A dead controller cannot be told from a quiet one: during a worker phase, 28 minutes without events is normal (live-status:no-liveness-indicator). - A run the controller stopped before freeze, or interrupted during review or freeze, shows no cause and no command. Its reason is only in a node-less controller row that no page renders (live-status:run-why-not-surfaced, live-status:no-next-action). - Every workflow is titled "Feature implementation" (orientation:naming-feature-implementation). - Reaching a run takes three clicks through near-empty pages (orientation:hierarchy-depth-empty-levels). All 23 P1 findings fall into these four themes. Appendix A maps all 72 findings. ## 2. Goals and non-goals ### Goals 1. **Answer first.** The first screen of a run page, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, answers five questions: - Where is the run, or where did it stop? - Why? - Since when? - What exactly do I type next, if anything? - Is this page current? 2. **One story in time.** At 1440×900 the first screen also shows the Steps table: each step's start, duration and attempt markers. The markers include ⚑ (the controller's diagnosis) and ⚒ (an operator repair) on the step they concern. - The full text of the node-less diagnosis and repair rows is in Activity, directly below Steps on the same default tab, never behind a toggle or a tab. - The guarantee covers runs with up to 2 lanes: every live run so far, and every fixture except `RUN_THREE_LANES`. For those runs the focus step's row is inside the fold; section 4.2 has the measured budget. - With 3 or more lanes the graph grows a row and the focus row can fall below the fold. The Now banner still names the focus step there. - At 390×844 the first screen holds the Now banner, and Steps follow directly. 3. **One home per piece of evidence.** Each piece of evidence is shown once, where it answers its question: files on the worker, checks, logs and screenshots on verification, findings on review. Everywhere else it appears as a one-line link or a count. 4. **Short node pages.** A node page's first screen shows its verdict, timing, attempts and a section index with counts. Long lists are collapsed and fetch their content only on demand. No node page needs more than about 3 screens before the operator expands something. 5. **Live-watch trust.** A freshness chip is always visible. - While a run is running or paused, the chip also says whether its controller process is alive (B2 `activity.controller`; Linux `/proc`, and "unknown" elsewhere). - A worker or reviewer that waits on the operator is visible on the run page, the graph, the Steps and strip rows, the run lists and the browser tab title. That covers a waiting question and a pane that needs attention. 6. **Honesty kept, said once.** The rules survive: a worker's success is not workflow completion, a worker's report is as signalled and not verified, the viewer is read-only, executors are marked, inferred times are marked. Each is said once, compactly. 7. **Shippable slices.** The existing browser suite stays green in both phases (worker mocks and candidate seeds), apart from assertions this PRD migrates explicitly in the same slice. ### Non-goals - Starting, answering, approving, retrying, repairing or cancelling anything from the viewer. Commands are shown as text to copy. - Changing the controller, exporter or event vocabulary (`workflow/*.py`). Those gaps are follow-ups C1–C10. Until they land, the viewer infers the missing values and labels every inference. - A liveness claim from PID existence alone, such as `process.kill(pid, 0)` on a PID parsed from event text. PID reuse would give a false "alive". - B2 instead reads `/proc//cmdline` and the process start time. It says "running" only for this run's own `automatic-step` child, started before it logged its PID. It says "unknown" whenever it cannot tell. - A controller heartbeat (C7) would make this portable. - The Pi/Claude skills areas. - Renaming `definition.name`. It feeds `definition_revision` (server/projectsConfig.ts:89-90), so changing it would flag every old run as "definition changed". ### Confirmed decisions - **The SVG graph stays.** It is fitted to the width by retuning `dag.ts`, not rebuilt as HTML. `.workflow-node-meta`, the aria-label format, `.workflow-node-shape` `stroke-dasharray`, `.is-agent`/`.is-controller` and arrow-key roving are unchanged (clarity.spec.ts:63-109, projects.spec.ts:164-168). - **A one-row Projects header.** On Projects routes the app header is one 48 px row: title, the Pi/Claude/Projects roots and Refresh. The Pi/Claude subtitle is dropped there. The breadcrumb is the only other chrome (28 px). Today the chrome takes about 150 px, or about 180 px with the info line (`04-…-fold.png`). The skills routes keep their header. - **Tabs above the graph.** `[Run] [Assignment]` sit directly under the Now banner. The graph lives inside the Run tabpanel, so it disappears on Assignment and comes back on Run (inputs.spec.ts:56, :89). - **One pipeline view per screen.** On the run page, the graph shows *shape and status* and the Steps table shows *time*. The Steps table is the `run-node-list`, not "the same graph as text". On node pages a sticky step strip replaces the graph, so the graph and the strip never share a screen. 42	  for (const span of timeline.byNode.get(nodeId) ?? []) groups.set(span.attempt, [...(groups.get(span.attempt) ?? []), span])

102	 * header links it only once one of them loads. Empty for a step with one attempt or none.
103	 */
104	export function attemptStrip(detail: RunDetail, timeline: Timeline, nodeId: string): StripItem[] {
105	  const groups = attemptsOf(timeline, nodeId)
106	  if (groups.size < 2) return []
107	  const uris = attemptResultUris(detail, nodeId)
108	  const items: StripItem[] = [...groups.entries()].map(([attempt, spans]) => {
109	    const start = earliest(spans.map(span => span.start))
110	    const live = spans.some(span => span.live)
111	    const end = live ? null : latest(spans.map(span => span.end))
112	    const chip: AttemptChip = {
113	      attempt, status: attemptStatus(spans), start, ms: start && end ? Math.max(0, ms(end) - ms(start)) : null,
114	      outcome: spans.map(span => span.outcome).filter(Boolean).join('; '),
115	      reason: '',
116	      uris: uris.filter(item => item.attempt === attempt).map(item => item.uri),
117	    }
118	    return { kind: 'attempt', at: (start ?? end)?.at ?? '', chip }
119	  })
120	  let previous: AttemptChip | null = null
121	  for (const item of items) {
122	    if (item.kind !== 'attempt') continue
123	    const { chip } = item
124	    if (chip.status === 'failed' && chip.outcome) {
125	      chip.reason = previous?.status === 'failed' && previous.outcome === chip.outcome ? 'same' : reasonWords(chip.outcome)
126	    }
127	    previous = chip
128	  }
129	  for (const marker of timeline.markers) {
130	    if (marker.node_id !== nodeId || (marker.kind !== 'diagnosis' && marker.kind !== 'repair')) continue
131	    items.push({ kind: marker.kind, at: marker.at, label: marker.kind === 'repair' ? `repair ${marker.repair?.n ?? ''}`.trim() : 'diagnosis', message: marker.message })
132	  }
133	  return items.sort((a, b) => (Date.parse(a.at) || 0) - (Date.parse(b.at) || 0))
134	}
135	
136	/**
137	 * The cause a header names after its status (8): a failure's own error first; on an earlier attempt's page, that attempt's
138	 * outcome as the timeline re-read it (served events may all carry one attempt number, 5.2 rule 1); otherwise the latest
139	 * status message of the attempt, humanized. Null when nothing recorded one.
140	 */
141	export function causeOf({ timeline, nodeId, attempt, events, latest, error }: {
142	  timeline: Timeline | null
143	  nodeId: string
144	  /** The viewed earlier attempt; null for the latest. */
145	  attempt: number | null
146	  /** The node's events; the latest attempt's are those of `latest`. */
147	  events: WorkflowEvent[]
148	  latest: number
149	  error: string | null
150	}): string | null {
151	  if (error) return error
152	  if (attempt !== null && timeline !== null) {
153	    const outcome = (attemptsOf(timeline, nodeId).get(attempt) ?? []).map(span => span.outcome).filter(Boolean).join('; ')
154	    if (outcome) return outcome
155	  }
156	  const shown = attempt ?? latest
157	  const own = events.filter(event => event.status !== null && (event.attempt === shown || shown === 0))
158	  // Only the latest attempt falls back to the node's last status message; an earlier one never quotes a later attempt.
159	  const last = own.at(-1) ?? (attempt === null ? events.findLast(event => event.status !== null) : undefined)
160	  return last ? humanizeEvent(last) : null
161	}
162	
163	/** A failure's reasons in a few words: the checks its keyed gate reasons name ("unit, integration"), else the outcome itself. */
164	function reasonWords(outcome: string): string {
165	  const segments = outcome.split(';').map(segment => segment.trim()).filter(Boolean)
166	  const keys = segments.map(segment => /^([\w.-]+):\s/.exec(segment)?.[1] ?? null)
167	  return keys.length > 0 && keys.every(key => key !== null) ? [...new Set(keys)].join(', ') : outcome
168	}
169	
170	/**
171	 * Which attempt of a verification this is on its revision (5.3): counted from the operator's latest repair before it, since
172	 * a repair restarts the attempt cap. Without a repair it is the attempt itself.
173	 */
174	export function revisionAttempt(timeline: Timeline, nodeId: string, attempt: number): number {
175	  const groups = attemptsOf(timeline, nodeId)
176	  const at = (value: number) => {
177	    const spans = groups.get(value) ?? []
178	    const instant = earliest(spans.map(span => span.start)) ?? earliest(spans.map(span => span.end))
179	    return instant ? ms(instant) : null
180	  }
181	  const shown = at(attempt)
182	  if (shown === null) return attempt
183	  const repaired = timeline.markers
184	    .filter(marker => marker.kind === 'repair' && marker.node_id === nodeId && Date.parse(marker.at) <= shown)
185	    .reduce((last, marker) => Math.max(last, Date.parse(marker.at)), -Infinity)
186	  if (repaired === -Infinity) return attempt
187	  return [...groups.keys()].filter(value => value <= attempt && (at(value) ?? shown) >= repaired).length
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * Dedup by `result_uri` (7): when a launch node and a verify node link the same result, the verify node shows its facts
192	 * (status, session, commits, the gate's error) and the launch node the worker's narrative (summary, assumptions). A result
193	 * no other node links keeps both.
194	 */
195	export function resultRole(detail: RunDetail, nodeId: string): ResultRole {
196	  const nodes = detail.snapshot.nodes
197	  const node = nodes.find(candidate => candidate.node_id === nodeId)
198	  const uri = node?.result_uri ?? null
199	  const kind = detail.definition.nodes.find(candidate => candidate.node_id === nodeId)?.kind
200	  if (uri === null || (kind !== 'worker' && kind !== 'verification')) return { facts: true, narrative: true, partner: null }
201	  const partnerKind = kind === 'worker' ? 'verification' : 'worker'
202	  const partner = nodes.find(candidate => candidate.node_id !== nodeId && candidate.result_uri === uri && candidate.kind === partnerKind)?.node_id ?? null
203	  if (partner === null) return { facts: true, narrative: true, partner: null }
204	  return kind === 'worker' ? { facts: false, narrative: true, partner } : { facts: true, narrative: false, partner }
205	}
206	
207	// ---- The section index (4.4, 7) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
208	
209	/** One section of a node page: its anchor key, its name in the index and, when it lists items, how many. */
210	export type SectionEntry = { key: string; label: string; count?: number }
211	
212	export const sectionId = (key: string) => `node-section-${key}`
213	
214	/** What one verified result holds, sorted the way its sections show it. */
215	export function evidenceOf(result: WorkerResult) {
216	  const artifactsById = new Map(result.artifacts.map(artifact => [artifact.artifact_id, artifact]))
217	  const checkLogs = new Set(result.checks.map(check => check.log_artifact_id))
218	  const screenshots = result.artifacts.filter(artifact => artifact.kind === 'screenshot')
219	  // Check logs are shown with their check and captured files on the launch node; everything else that is not a screenshot is listed here.
220	  const others = result.artifacts.filter(artifact => artifact.kind !== 'screenshot' && artifact.kind !== 'file' && !checkLogs.has(artifact.artifact_id))
221	  // Checks the gate recorded on this isolated snapshot but gates only at the combined candidate (build, browser).
222	  const deferred = new Map((result.deferred_checks ?? []).map(entry => [entry.check_index, entry.id]))
223	  const passed = result.status === 'succeeded' && result.error === null
224	  return { artifactsById, screenshots, others, deferred, passed }
225	}
226	
227	/**
228	 * The index entries of a verified result's sections: only those with something in them. A verify node whose lane the run's
229	 * inputs name lists its Requirements before the Result.
230	 */
231	export function verifiedSections(result: WorkerResult, options: { requirements?: boolean } = {}): SectionEntry[] {
232	  const { screenshots, others, deferred } = evidenceOf(result)
233	  return [
234	    { key: 'gate', label: 'Gate' },
235	    ...(result.checks.length > 0 ? [{ key: 'checks', label: 'Checks', count: result.checks.length }] : []),
236	    ...(screenshots.length > 0 || deferred.size > 0 ? [{ key: 'screenshots', label: 'Screenshots', count: screenshots.length }] : []),
237	    ...(others.length > 0 ? [{ key: 'artifacts', label: 'Artifacts', count: others.length }] : []),
238	    ...(options.requirements ? [{ key: 'requirements', label: 'Requirements' }] : []),
239	    { key: 'result', label: 'Result' },
240	  ]
241	}

1	/**
2	 * The fixture extension point of the viewer UX slices (docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md section 11). Each slice adds its runs in its
3	 * own module, `ux-<slice>.ts`, as a new workflow `ux-<slice>` appended after every workflow of `PROJECT`, so the existing
4	 * counts (two projects, five runs in `feature-flow`) do not change:
5	 * - `payloads`: the contract payloads the worker-phase mocks serve. This module spreads them into the maps `fixtures.ts`
6	 *   exports when it is first imported; `mock.ts` imports it, so they are merged before any request is served.
7	 * - `seed`: writes the same logical runs for the candidate phase and returns their registry entries; `seedCandidate`
8	 *   calls every module's seed with a `SeedContext`, appends the entries to `PROJECT`'s workflows and adds any top-level
9	 *   registry keys a module returns (S6's `viewer.expose_run_dir`, once the server accepts it).
10	 * After S1 no slice edits `fixtures.ts`, `mock.ts` or `seed.ts`: a slice changes only its own module. Modules import the
11	 * builders `fixtures.ts` exports and only types from here and from `seed.ts`, so no import cycle exists.
12	 */
13	import type { ReviewResult, RunDetail, RunInputs, WorkflowDefinition } from '../../../contracts/projects/v1.ts'
14	import type { WorkerResult, WorkflowEvent } from '../../../contracts/workflow/v1.ts'
15	import {
16	  artifactFiles, PROJECT, reviewResults, runDetails, runEvents, runInputs, runLists, workerResults, workflowLists,
17	  type ArtifactFile, type DefinitionNode,
18	} from '../fixtures.ts'
19	import type { SeedContext } from '../seed.ts'
20	import { uxLaunch } from './ux-launch.ts'
21	import { uxLists } from './ux-lists.ts'
22	import { uxNode } from './ux-node.ts'
23	import { uxReview } from './ux-review.ts'
24	import { uxRun } from './ux-run.ts'
25	import { uxTime } from './ux-time.ts'
26	import { uxVerify } from './ux-verify.ts'
27	
28	/** A module's worker-phase payloads, keyed like the maps of `fixtures.ts`; run lists are derived from `runDetails`. */
29	export type UxPayloads = {
30	  /** Registered after every existing workflow of `PROJECT`, in module order. */
31	  workflows: WorkflowDefinition[]
32	  runDetails: Record<string, RunDetail>
33	  runEvents: Record<string, WorkflowEvent[]>
34	  /** Per run, keyed `<node>/<attempt>` or `candidate_<lane>/<attempt>` like the results route. */
35	  workerResults: Record<string, Record<string, WorkerResult>>
36	  reviewResults: Record<string, ReviewResult>
37	  runInputs: Record<string, RunInputs>
38	  artifactFiles: Record<string, ArtifactFile[]>
39	}
40	
41	/** One registry workflow entry, as `seedCandidate` writes them. */
42	export type RegistryWorkflow = { workflow_id: string; runs_root: string; definition: { name: string; nodes: DefinitionNode[] } }
43	
44	/** What a module's candidate-phase seed adds to the registry. */
45	export type UxSeed = {
46	  workflows: RegistryWorkflow[]
47	  /** Top-level registry keys beside `version` and `projects`; a later module's key replaces an earlier one's. */
48	  registry?: Record<string, unknown>
49	}
50	
51	export type UxFixtureModule = {
52	  payloads?: Partial<UxPayloads>
53	  seed?: (context: SeedContext) => UxSeed
54	}
55	
56	/** In slice order; the order the added workflows are listed in, in both phases. */
57	export const UX_FIXTURE_MODULES: readonly UxFixtureModule[] = [uxTime, uxRun, uxNode, uxVerify, uxLaunch, uxReview, uxLists]
58	
59	function mergePayloads(modules: readonly UxFixtureModule[]) {
60	  for (const { payloads = {} } of modules) {
61	    const workflows = payloads.workflows ?? []
62	    workflowLists[PROJECT.project_id].workflows.push(...workflows)
63	    Object.assign(runDetails, payloads.runDetails)
64	    Object.assign(runEvents, payloads.runEvents)
65	    Object.assign(workerResults, payloads.workerResults)
66	    Object.assign(reviewResults, payloads.reviewResults)
67	    Object.assign(runInputs, payloads.runInputs)
68	    Object.assign(artifactFiles, payloads.artifactFiles)
69	    // The mocks index these per run: a run without events, results or artifacts serves none rather than failing.
70	    for (const runId of Object.keys(payloads.runDetails ?? {})) {
71	      runEvents[runId] ??= []
72	      workerResults[runId] ??= {}
73	      artifactFiles[runId] ??= []
74	    }
75	    // Each workflow's runs sorted by `updated_at` descending then `run_id` ascending, as the contract requires.
76	    for (const workflow of workflows) {
77	      runLists[workflow.workflow_id] = {
78	        runs: Object.values(runDetails).map(detail => detail.summary).filter(summary => summary.workflow_id === workflow.workflow_id)
79	          .sort((a, b) => b.updated_at.localeCompare(a.updated_at) || a.run_id.localeCompare(b.run_id)),
80	        next_cursor: null,
81	      }
82	    }
83	  }
84	}
85	
86	mergePayloads(UX_FIXTURE_MODULES)
87	
88	/** Seeds every module's runs for the candidate phase; returns what to add to the registry, in module order. */
89	export function seedUxFixtures(context: SeedContext): Required<UxSeed> {
90	  const seeded = UX_FIXTURE_MODULES.map(module => module.seed?.(context) ?? { workflows: [] })
91	  return {
92	    workflows: seeded.flatMap(seed => seed.workflows),
93	    registry: Object.assign({}, ...seeded.map(seed => seed.registry ?? {})) as Record<string, unknown>,
94	  }
95	}

1	/**
2	 * Per-reviewer wording for the review node. A review result always carries `reviewers`, one entry per reviewer the run
3	 * declared (one named `review` for exports recorded before the list existed, filled by the adapter), so nothing here has
4	 * a single-reviewer case: the combined verdict is unanimous, and a blocked run is explained by the reviewers that caused it.
5	 * Pure helpers, kept out of the component file so it only exports components.
6	 */
7	import { isBlockingFinding, type ReviewFinding, type ReviewResult } from './api.ts'
8	
9	export type Reviewer = ReviewResult['reviewers'][number]
10	
11	const SEVERITIES: readonly ReviewFinding['severity'][] = ['P0', 'P1', 'P2']
12	
13	/**
14	 * How a reviewer ended, in the contract's vocabulary (`REVIEWER_STATUSES` in `contracts/projects/v1.ts`): `accepted` (its
15	 * completion file was accepted), `blocked` (its verdict, an unresolved P0/P1, a rejected file or the review deadline
16	 * blocked the run), `superseded` (stopped after the run was decided while it was still working) or `pending` (no verdict
17	 * recorded yet). The contract records no separate status for the deadline or a rejected file: both are `blocked` with a
18	 * null verdict, so the wording for them is derived from `verdict` in `blockingReason`, never from an invented status.
19	 */
20	const STATUS_WORDING: Readonly<Record<Reviewer['status'], string>> = {
21	  accepted: 'completion file accepted',
22	  blocked: 'blocked',
23	  superseded: 'stopped after the combined decision',
24	  pending: 'no verdict recorded yet',
25	}
26	
27	export function statusWording(status: Reviewer['status']): string {
28	  return STATUS_WORDING[status]
29	}
30	
31	/** Whether the reviewer was stopped because of another reviewer's outcome rather than its own. */
32	function superseded(reviewer: Pick<Reviewer, 'status'>): boolean {
33	  return reviewer.status === 'superseded'
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * Why this reviewer's own outcome blocks the run, or null when it does not: a blocked verdict; an approval that left an
38	 * unresolved P0/P1; or a blocked status without any verdict, which the contract records for both the expired review
39	 * deadline and a rejected completion file (it does not say which).
40	 */
41	export function blockingReason(reviewer: Pick<Reviewer, 'status' | 'verdict' | 'findings'>): string | null {
42	  if (reviewer.verdict === 'blocked') return 'blocked the candidate'
43	  if (reviewer.verdict === 'approved') return reviewer.findings.some(isBlockingFinding) ? 'approved with an unresolved P0/P1 finding' : null
44	  if (reviewer.status === 'blocked') return 'delivered no verdict: the review deadline expired or its completion file was rejected'
45	  return null
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * One line for the reviewer strip: how the reviewer ended, with the blocking reason when it has one. A reviewer without a
50	 * verdict says so: superseded before deciding, pending and not yet launched, or pending after its launch.
51	 */
52	export function outcomeWording(reviewer: Pick<Reviewer, 'status' | 'verdict' | 'findings' | 'launched_at'>): string {
53	  const reason = blockingReason(reviewer)
54	  if (reason !== null) return reason
55	  if (superseded(reviewer)) return reviewer.verdict === null ? `${statusWording(reviewer.status)}, no verdict` : statusWording(reviewer.status)
56	  if (reviewer.status === 'pending') return reviewer.launched_at === null ? 'not launched, no verdict recorded yet' : statusWording(reviewer.status)
57	  return statusWording(reviewer.status)
58	}
59	
60	/** "1 P1, 2 P2" in severity order, listing only the severities present; "no findings" when the list is empty. */
61	export function severityCounts(findings: readonly Pick<ReviewFinding, 'severity'>[]): string {

test(`[scenario:legacy-run] A stored 1.2.0 two-lane export renders as before without re-export (${phase})`, async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  // The two-lane workflow still lists exactly its own five runs; the lanes workflow is a separate entry.
  await page.goto(workflowUrl(PROJECT.project_id, WORKFLOW_ID))
  await expect(page.getByTestId('run-list').locator('li')).toHaveCount(5)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('run-list').locator(`[data-run-id="${RUN_THREE_LANES}"]`)).toHaveCount(0)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('current-definition')).toContainText(`${GRAPH_NODES.length} nodes`)
  await page.goto(`/projects/${PROJECT.project_id}`)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('workflows-list').getByRole('link')).toContainText([WORKFLOW_NAME, LANES_WORKFLOW_NAME])

  // The pinned two-lane graph: the same nine nodes with their stored labels, no third lane anywhere.
  await page.goto(runUrl(RUN_SUCCEEDED))
  await expect(page.getByTestId('run-view')).toHaveAttribute('data-run-status', 'succeeded')
  await expect(graphNodes(page)).toHaveCount(GRAPH_NODES.length)
  expect(await attributeList(graphNodes(page), 'data-graph-node')).toEqual(GRAPH_NODES.map(node => node.node_id))
  await expect(graphNode(page, 'launch_ui')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', /^Launch UI worker, worker, succeeded, attempt 1/)

175	function writeRun(runsRoot: string, repository: string, runId: string, options: RunOptions) {
176	  const runDir = join(runsRoot, runId)
177	  mkdirSync(runDir, { recursive: true })
178	  const inputs = options.inputs ?? null
179	  const version = options.version ?? '1.2.0'
180	  const lanes = options.lanes ?? ['ui', 'adapter']
181	  const pinnedTask = (lane: string) => inputs?.workers[lane]?.task ?? (lane === 'ui' ? uiTask(leakFor(runsRoot, runId)) : lane === 'adapter' ? adapterTask() : docsTask())
182	  const plan = {
183	    run_id: runId, repository, base_commit: BASE_COMMIT, allow_edits: true,
184	    nodes: Object.fromEntries(lanes.map(lane => [lane, { worktree: join(runDir, `worktree-${lane}`), task: pinnedTask(lane), session_id: LANE_SESSIONS[lane], observed_start_commit: BASE_COMMIT }])),
185	    ...(version === '1.3.0' || version === '1.4.0' || version === '1.5.0' ? { workers: [...lanes], excluded_workers: inputs?.excluded_workers ?? [] } : {}),
186	    ...(options.reviewers ? { reviewers: options.reviewers.map(reviewer => ({ reviewer_id: reviewer, prompt: `Review the candidate as the ${reviewer} reviewer.` })) } : {}),
187	    mode: 'live', policy_sha256: 'e'.repeat(64), created_at: options.createdAt, source_branch: inputs?.source_branch ?? 'feature/synthetic',
188	    ...(inputs === null || inputs.automatic !== null ? { automatic: inputs?.automatic ?? { worker_timeout_seconds: 14400, review_timeout_seconds: 1800 } } : {}),
189	  }
190	  writeJson(join(runDir, 'plan.json'), plan)
191	  writeFileSync(join(runDir, 'events.jsonl'), options.events.map(event => JSON.stringify(event)).join('\n') + '\n')
192	  if (options.diff !== undefined) writeFileSync(join(runDir, 'review.diff'), options.diff)
193	  const packets = options.packets(runDir)
194	  const state = {
195	    version, run_id: runId, base_commit: BASE_COMMIT, created_at: options.createdAt,
196	    definition: { name: options.definitionName ?? WORKFLOW_NAME, nodes: options.definitionNodes },
197	    values: { run_id: runId, ...options.values }, next: options.next, tasks: options.tasks, events: options.events,
198	    verification_packets: packets, updated_at: options.updatedAt,
199	    ...(version !== '1.0.0' ? { review: options.review ?? null, inputs } : {}),
200	  }
201	  writeJson(join(runDir, 'run-state.json'), state)
202	  return runDir
203	}
204	
205	/** A real absolute path under the run directory that the raw seeded texts name; the adapter must redact it. */
206	function leakFor(runsRoot: string, runId: string): string {
207	  return join(runsRoot, runId, 'worktree-ui', 'test-results')
208	}

64	export function RunView({ scope, detail, current, selectedNodeId, selectedAttempt = null, tab, refreshToken, pollToken = 0, freshness, onNavigate, onAnnounce }: Props) {
65	  const { summary, definition, snapshot } = detail
66	  const clock = useNow(summary.status !== 'succeeded' && summary.status !== 'cancelled')

63	  attention: z.strictObject({ kind: z.enum(ATTENTION_KINDS), node_id: id.nullable(), since: timestamp.nullable() }).nullable(),

  await expect(page.getByTestId('task-required-kinds')).toHaveText('Required check kinds for this lane: unit')

  await expect(findingRows(page)).toHaveCount(6)
  for (const finding of reviewFindings(RUN_SUCCEEDED)) await expect(findings(page)).toContainText(finding.message)
  await page.getByTestId('group-by-worker').click()
  const groups = findings(page).locator('section[data-worker-group]')
  await expect(groups).toHaveCount(4)
  expect(await attributeList(groups, 'data-worker-group')).toEqual(['ui', 'adapter', 'multiple', 'none'])
  await expect(workerGroup(page, 'ui').getByRole('heading')).toHaveText('Worker ui (3)')
  await expect(workerGroup(page, 'adapter').getByRole('heading')).toHaveText('Worker adapter (1)')
  await expect(workerGroup(page, 'multiple').getByRole('heading')).toHaveText('Multiple workers (1)')
  await expect(workerGroup(page, 'none').getByRole('heading')).toHaveText('No worker (cross-cutting) (1)')
  const legacy = workerGroup(page, 'multiple').getByTestId('finding')
  await expect(legacy).toHaveAttribute('data-worker', 'both')
  await expect(workerColumn(legacy)).toHaveText('multiple workers')
  await expect(workerColumn(workerGroup(page, 'ui').getByTestId('finding').first())).toHaveText('ui')
  await expect(findings(page)).not.toContainText('Both workers')
  await expect(findings(page)).toContainText('Workers are the lanes this run had (ui, adapter)')
  await expect(page.getByTestId('finding-task-link')).toHaveCount(3)
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="finding-task-link"][data-lane="ui"]')).toHaveCount(2)

concerns.message: Rule 1 of the workflow title rule (the latest run's `activity.feature`) renames the existing fixture workflows in the candidate phase. That contradicts the constraint that `currentCrumb` assertions stay unchanged. The PRD's claim that the fixture names are not generic only covers rules 2 and 3. In the candidate phase the server serves `activity.feature = run.inputs?.feature` (server/projects.ts:1028). Every seeded `feature-flow` run has inputs (seed.ts:282-347), with `feature: FEATURE_NAME = 'Review visibility and run inputs in the viewer'` (fixtures.ts:1275), while WORKFLOW_NAME is 'Feature flow'. Today `workflowTitle` (status.ts:67) applies only rules 2 and 3, which is why the suite is green.
concerns.consequence: Once the lists lane adds rule 1 to crumbs and headings, these fail in the candidate phase: projects.spec.ts:138 and :181 (`currentCrumb toHaveText(WORKFLOW_NAME)`), :135 and :136 (the workflows-list texts and the click by `^Feature flow`), and :149 (`Current definition graph of Feature flow`). So does lanes.spec.ts:182 (`workflows-list` toContainText [WORKFLOW_NAME, LANES_WORKFLOW_NAME]), and neither lane owns lanes.spec.ts, so it cannot be migrated. The worker-phase mocks serve no `activity`, so the lane passes its own worker run and then fails the verifier's candidate run. That leaves a choice between breaking the rule, a blocked lane, or editing a file outside its ownership.

concerns.message: The lists lane owns LiveStatus.tsx, NowBanner.tsx and CommandBlock.tsx, but none of them receives `activity` or `run_dir`. LiveStatus gets `{status, meta, now}` from RunHeader.tsx:89/138. NowBanner gets `{now, clock, focusHref}` from RunView.tsx:212. CommandBlock gets `{next}` from NowBanner, NodeHeader.tsx:194 and WorkerInputs.tsx:318. RunView.tsx and RunHeader.tsx belong to neither lane. The only owned path to the data is ProjectsView.tsx, which renders RunView with `detail`.
concerns.consequence: A worker that threads props will edit RunHeader.tsx or RunView.tsx and fail the ownership check. A worker that improvises may use a module-level side channel in api.ts. The `served-activity` scenario (the controller chip and the `RUN=` line) cannot be met through the existing props. The clean route is a React context provided in ProjectsView, following the `TimeReferenceContext` precedent in useNow.ts:117, and the task should say so. That route also puts the `RUN=` line into `node-next` and the answer blocks, which is intended but changes what the panels lane's `node-next` shows in worker-phase mocks for exposed runs.

concerns.message: Moving ReviewPanel onto `useRunReview` (as decisions.md requires) drops two behaviours of ReviewDetail.tsx:347-353. The first is the fallback path `paths.review(scope, attempt)` for exports whose review node has no `result_uri`. The second is the resource key that includes `node.status`, which re-asks when the node's status changes. The cache also stores `orNotRecorded`'s null as `ready`, and a `ready` entry is never re-fetched (useRunData.ts:51).
concerns.consequence: If NodeDetail passes only `result_uri`, as RunView.tsx:80 does, older exports without a link lose their review and show 'review-none'. If it passes the fallback path, a review node opened before its verdict caches null and keeps showing 'No review recorded' after the review lands, until a manual Refresh. That is a live-watch regression that no current test covers.

concerns.message: Only the `finding` test id is protected for the blocking card. Several other page-wide or exact-text assertions depend on what the card and the reviewer durations reuse: `page.getByTestId('finding-task-link')` toHaveCount(3) (inputs.spec.ts:193, lanes.spec.ts:140 and :239), page-level `review-verdict` and `review-blocked-by` toHaveText (review.spec.ts:109-115, reviewers.spec.ts:139-141), and exact `reviewer-status` text (reviewers.spec.ts:68, 148, 154).
concerns.consequence: If the card reuses FindingRow's requirement or file links, or adds a second `review-verdict`, the blocked-run assertions hit strict-mode or count failures. The three `finding-task-link` counts are on approved runs, so they survive only because those runs have no blocking card. Adding 'took 3m49s' or 'no verdict' inside `reviewer-status` breaks the exact-text checks, so durations must stay in their own element (as ReviewDetail.tsx:167 already does).

concerns.message: The reviewer strip already shows 'took <span>' from `launched_at` to `accepted_at` (ReviewDetail.tsx:155-167). The pending wording already contains 'no verdict recorded yet' (reviewers.ts:24).
concerns.consequence: Parts of `review-blocking-first` pass against the pre-change code, so the red run will not fail for those parts. The handoff's red evidence should name the assertions that actually fail (blocking card position, 'launch time not recorded', the 390 px cards), or it will look as if the test cannot detect the change.

This fixes the live "Feature implementation" problem the PRD targets, keeps every `currentCrumb`, `workflows-list` and 'Current definition graph of …' assertion green in both phases, and needs no change to lanes.spec.ts, which no lane owns. Record it in decisions.md as an operator choice.
